health.title: Plant health
health.disclaimer: PlantCare does not diagnose diseases. The same symptom can have several causes: observe the whole plant and its conditions, and ask a nursery or a local expert if in doubt.
health.newActionPlaceholder: e.g. Moved away from the window

healthGuide.title: Plant problems guide
healthGuide.disclaimer: One symptom can have several causes, sometimes combined. Use these leads to observe your plant, change one thing at a time, and ask a professional if the problem persists.
healthGuide.sources: Based on general guidance from the Royal Horticultural Society and university extension services.

overwatering.title: Too much water
overwatering.body: Soil that stays wet deprives roots of air. Often lower leaves yellow first and the soil smells musty.

underwatering.title: Not enough water
underwatering.body: Dry, shrinking soil and limp, crispy leaves. Water thoroughly, then adjust the frequency.

natural_ageing.title: Natural ageing
natural_ageing.body: The oldest, lowest leaves yellow and drop from time to time. If only one leaf at a time is affected, it is usually normal.

low_light.title: Not enough light
low_light.body: Pale leaves, long stretched stems and slow growth. Move the plant gradually to a brighter spot.

nutrient_deficiency.title: Nutrient deficiency
nutrient_deficiency.body: Can cause uniform yellowing or slow growth, especially after a long time without repotting or feeding. Follow the fertilizer label.

sudden_change.title: Sudden change
sudden_change.body: A move, draught or temperature change can make a plant drop or yellow some leaves while it adapts.

low_humidity.title: Dry air
low_humidity.body: Brown, crispy leaf tips are common near heaters or in dry climates for humidity-loving plants.

sunburn.title: Sunburn
sunburn.body: Pale or brown patches on the side facing the sun, often after moving a plant into direct sun too quickly.

salt_buildup.title: Mineral or fertilizer build-up
salt_buildup.body: White crust on the soil and brown leaf edges. Flush the soil with plenty of water and avoid over-fertilizing.

cold_damage.title: Cold damage
cold_damage.body: Dark, soft or translucent patches after exposure to cold or frost.

root_rot.title: Root rot
root_rot.body: Brown, mushy, bad-smelling roots, usually from waterlogged soil. The plant may wilt even when the soil is wet.

heat_stress.title: Heat stress
heat_stress.body: Leaves droop in the hottest hours and may recover in the evening. Provide shade and check moisture.

transplant_shock.title: Transplant shock
transplant_shock.body: Temporary wilting after repotting or planting out. Keep conditions stable while the roots settle.

pot_bound.title: Pot too small
pot_bound.body: Roots circling or coming out of the drainage holes, water running straight through. Repot when the season allows.

poor_drainage.title: Poor drainage
poor_drainage.body: A pot without holes or a compact substrate keeps water around the roots.

spider_mites.title: Spider mites
spider_mites.body: Tiny dots on leaves, fine webbing and dull, speckled foliage, more frequent in dry air.

mealybugs.title: Mealybugs
mealybugs.body: White, cottony clusters in leaf joints and under leaves.

scale.title: Scale insects
scale.body: Small brown bumps on stems and leaf veins, sometimes with sticky residue.

aphids.title: Aphids
aphids.body: Small green, black or white insects on young shoots and buds.

fungus_gnats.title: Fungus gnats
fungus_gnats.body: Small black flies around the soil, linked to soil that stays moist.

thrips.title: Thrips
thrips.body: Silvery streaks and tiny black dots on leaves.

powdery_mildew.title: Powdery mildew
powdery_mildew.body: White, powdery coating on leaves, favoured by poor air flow.

leaf_spot.title: Leaf spots
leaf_spot.body: Brown or black spots, sometimes with a yellow halo. Can be fungal or bacterial, or caused by water on leaves.

grey_mould.title: Grey mould
grey_mould.body: Fuzzy grey growth on soft tissues or flowers in cool, damp conditions.

dormancy.title: Seasonal rest
dormancy.body: Many plants grow little in winter or during dry seasons. This is normal.

many_factors.title: Many possible factors
many_factors.body: Note what you observe, recent changes and conditions in the journal: it will help you or an expert find the cause.

checks.soil_moisture: Feel the soil a few centimetres deep: is it soggy, damp or bone dry?
checks.drainage: Does the pot have drainage holes? Is water left standing in the saucer?
checks.which_leaves: Which leaves are affected: old lower leaves or new growth?
checks.recent_changes: Did anything change recently: place, season, watering, repotting?
checks.light_exposure: How much light does the plant get, and did it change?
checks.heat_sources: Is the plant near a heater, air conditioning or a draught?
checks.water_quality: Is the water very hard, or has the plant been fertilized a lot?
checks.roots: Gently remove the pot: are the roots firm and light, or brown and soft?
checks.temperature: Was the plant exposed to heat or cold?
checks.pot_size: Do roots fill the pot entirely?
checks.leaf_undersides: Inspect the undersides of leaves and stem joints with good light.
checks.isolate: Isolate the plant from the others while you investigate.
checks.neighbours: Check neighbouring plants for the same signs.
checks.air_flow: Is the air moving enough around the plant?
checks.wet_leaves: Do leaves stay wet for long after watering?
checks.remove_affected: Remove badly affected leaves with clean tools.
checks.season: Is it a resting season for this plant in your climate?
checks.ask_expert: If in doubt, ask a garden centre, a nursery or a local horticultural service.
